Therefore you see them in a narrow life, striving for something higher than their present state, knowing that the corruptions and innovations in their religion have corrupted for them what they have corrupted. Their progress will not be possible except by returning to the religion of nature. They are striving toward it, even if they do not perceive it, or they perceive it and feign ignorance. These are drops from the narrow life of two great nations, which adhere to two revealed books. So what is your opinion of the Magians and the idolaters and their countless sects? Their intelligent ones still seek to free themselves from them, because of the abundance of their superstitions and their harm to self, wealth and honour. Thus their people are in a wretchedness and torment to which no torment compares. As for whoever is saved from their calamities through Islam, he cannot be counted or enumerated.

Consider in the same way the group called the materialists, namely the atheists (dahriyyun) and the naturalists (tabi'iyyun). Without doubt they are the narrowest in breast, the most constricted in livelihood, the most agitated, and the greatest in division. It is not possible for two of them to hold one opinion. Rather, each of them imagines his god as he desires, and as his desires and passions depict it for him. Some of them said: "These people who confine their religion to a person knowing God and being upright in his deeds: when they are asked, 'What is the natural religion which you acknowledge?' they answer, 'It is that to which reason guides, free from revelation.' Then it is said to them: Reason, in itself, is weak, changing and deficient. It sees today as right what it sees tomorrow as wrong, and it judges today a matter to be lawful and permissible, and tomorrow it sees it as forbidden and not to be done. Its aims lead it to permit what pleases it, and make it recoil from what opposes its desires. So how can its possessor be upright in his deeds? What is the consistent and fixed standard of uprightness for these people? Each one sees himself, and it appears to him that he is upright! For example, the Chinese sees himself as upright even if he sells or kills his children. The Hindu sees this uprightness in himself even if he burns the woman upon the corpse of her husband. The idolater sees himself as upright even if he commits indecency in honour of Venus."

This is part 2 of al-Qasimi's commentary on verses 124–127 of Surah Ta-Ha (20).

Furthermore, most of the philosophers went astray in the sources from which they legislate, and they did not find the straight path of true uprightness. How can it be possible for common people that each one of them should have a "natural religion" (dīn ṭabī'ī) that he accepts however he wishes, that he shapes like a pliable thing, stretching it toward whatever pleases him and shortening it away from whatever he dislikes? Thus this religion differs according to the differences of intellects and desires among them. And how can we call something a fixed, general law (sharī'ah) when it is subject to the will and desires of each individual?

Even if we grant, for the sake of argument, that there exists someone who is naturally inclined to uprightness, justice and chastity, so that his nature leads him to that, what do we say about someone who is by nature fond of revenge, aggression and lusts? Especially since reason is weak and the soul commands evil, how can reason alone be a restraint against committing sins and crimes? Therefore Allah, glorified is He, did not decree a law for His creatures except out of mercy toward them, because of their weakness and their inclination toward evil. Human weakness and deviation require that he be bound by a law to which he submits. It is necessary for him as the system of the celestial bodies is necessary for them, and it is inseparable from him as speech, perception and freedom are inseparable, and as extension, weight, attraction and repulsion are necessary for inanimate bodies.

The first proof of the inseparability of the law from human nature is what a person finds within his soul and conscience of its being implanted in him in a theoretical implantation, so that he cannot strip himself of it. For example, how can a person, however much he may be blind to evil, strip himself of the conception (p-4222) that he is subject to a law that forbids him from killing, from embezzling the property of others, and from aggressing against them in any way? The law is written upon our hearts on tablets of flesh. Whoever investigates the general population of the earth finds that all tribes and peoples agree upon laws, even if they differ in some of their details. The freedom granted to man has only had its benefits restricted by laws and by submission to them. Otherwise it is a destruction of the order of the world, a calamity to good manners, and a plague upon what the Creator has planted in the minds of all people from the time of Adam until today. That is because it entails the corruption of human nature and the undermining of moral laws. For when a person knows that there is no God who rewards good and punishes evil, he unleashes the reins of corruption for his soul, casts off restraint in the arena of lusts and the acquisition of desires, pursuing what he thinks is his happiness, and believing that his soul is not immortal. His happiness has no object beyond this fleeting life.

It also entails the destruction of human society and the ruin of its prosperity. For after Allah, no covenant is observed among people, no sanctity is accorded to customs and laws, there is no piety toward kings, no justice toward subjects, no love, truthfulness, fidelity, or anything similar to these, which are essential in themselves for the maintenance of human harmony and the order of civilization.

In summary, let no one imagine that the world will endure, or that any order or social structure will remain in it, if people are not bound by a divine law that restrains the wicked from wickedness. Just as air is necessary for natural life, so the law is necessary for moral life. There is no life for living beings without air, and likewise there is no order or structure in the world without the law. End of quotation.

A scrupulous imam (Imam) said, in discussing the correction of belief and its necessity for the tranquility and happiness of the soul, the following in substance: We see before our eyes some people who have been granted great health and immense wealth, and who have been refined by various kinds of knowledge and learning, yet they are very prone to boredom and extremely perplexed. They can hardly feel at ease, nor do they take pleasure in any pleasure. It is as if there is pain in their pleasure, and for every joy there is a sorrow. They feel a gloom that has settled over their chests; they do not know its cause nor understand its reason. It is a gloom that does not leave them except by the removal of their minds (p-4223) from them, by a cup of pure wine. Therefore you see them extremely fond of it and greatly anguished at its loss, for it is their only remedy. What is the secret of this sleeplessness and boredom, despite this physical health and that financial wealth, which, as they claim, are the two matters upon which human happiness depends? What is this inner bewilderment and this conscientious loneliness, despite their refinement through various kinds of knowledge, which, as they claim, is the cure for people from the impulses of whispering?

Does this secret boredom not indicate to us that the soul yearns for something, and if a person's knowledge of it is absent, its effect has nonetheless guided him to it? That thing is not bodily health, nor abundance of wealth, nor a multitude of children, nor dwelling in palaces, nor eating various foods, nor listening to lutes, nor flirting with beautiful young women. Rather, it is another matter, in comparison to which these delights are counted as mere dust, and the worlds beside it are nothing but annihilation. What is this sublime matter which, if the soul obtains it, it becomes tranquil and calm, becomes enraptured and intoxicated by it, and is content and satisfied with it? It is without doubt soundness of belief. Here is the proof:

The soul is not of the nature of these deaf bodies, nor of the clay of this blind matter, such that it would become intimate with anything of these lowly earthly things or care for their pleasures, however great they may be. Rather, it is of a purely luminous nature. It is only at ease with a light that clears away from it the darknesses of dense earthly things, so that it may look over the exalted sanctuary of holiness and gaze upon its noble precincts. The soul is too exalted to be content with bodily desires, and too great to be satisfied with their adorned and transient pleasures. Therefore, however much a person deceives his soul by accumulating wealth and prosperity of condition, so that his inner self may find rest and his agitation may be stilled, the soul does not cease to establish proof upon proof against him, so that he may be guided to the clear path. If he reflects upon his matter, comprehends the truth of his inner self, and gives his soul its desired goal by bringing it the light it hopes for, his heart is calmed and his right guidance returns to him, even if his body is among spears and bullets, and his condition is one of poverty in the most wretched dwelling.

What, then, is the way to bring this wandering soul to its wish and to delight it with its aim, which is sound belief? The way to that is sound reason. Reason in the human species is one of its most excellent qualities and one of the finest gifts of Allah upon it, if it is used for what it was made for, and if its soundness and moderation are cared for. Through reason, a person sounds the depths of this great existence, despite the vastness of its parts and the immensity of its dimensions, and fathoms the course of the laws prevailing over it. Thereby one is guided to the existence of the Creator, mighty and majestic, and to the exaltation of His acts above futility and of His works above play. It is also through reason that one is guided to His knowledge, His management, His mercy and His wisdom, by evidence that is perceptible, admits no doubt, and is not tainted by suspicion. Through reason, a person studies the conditions of human communities, the laws of their rise and fall, and the causes of their elevation and debasement. He reflects on the conditions of the prophets whom Allah sent to His creation as guides and guidance. He deduces, by careful examination of what they brought and of the traces they left, the meaning of prophethood and its necessity for mankind. He also studies Allah's wisdom in the differences of faculties and perceptions, and in the diversity of religions and creeds. Through reason, a person distinguishes between the conditions of the past and the present, and accordingly differentiates between particular religions and universal religions. And with the support of knowledge and original reasoning, he arrives at the religion which must be the seal of all religions and remain as long as the human species remains, namely the law of the Seal of the Prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Fourth: I have seen words by Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, on this verse, in his two books al-Jawab al-Kafi and Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah. I wished to quote them here for their benefits and out of care for this verse, for it deserves that. He said in al-Jawab al-Kafi, in a section in which he clarified the punishments that result from sins: "Among them is a straitened life in this world and in the barzakh (intermediate state), and punishment in the Hereafter." He said: "The straitened life has been interpreted as the punishment of the grave. There is no doubt that it is among the straitened life. But the verse encompasses something more general than that, even though it is indefinite in the context of affirmation, for its generality is in meaning. For Allah, glorified is He, made the straitened life a consequence of turning away from His remembrance. So the one who turns away from Him has a share of the straitness of life in proportion to his turning away, even if he enjoys in this world all kinds of blessings. In his heart there is loneliness, humiliation, and sorrows that cut hearts, false hopes, and present punishment, all that it contains. Only the intoxications of lusts, passionate love, love of the world and of leadership conceal this from him, unless the intoxication of wine is added to them. The intoxication of these matters is greater than the intoxication of wine, for the one who drinks wine awakens and sobers up, but the intoxication of desire and love of the world does not leave its owner until he is intoxicated in the army of the dead. So the straitened life is necessary for whoever turns away from the remembrance of Allah which He sent down upon His Messenger (ﷺ), in this world, in the barzakh, and on the Day of Return. The eye is not comforted, the heart is not at rest, and the soul is not at peace, except through its God and its worshipped One, who is the Truth, while every other object of worship is false. Whoever finds comfort for his eye in Allah, every eye finds comfort in him. Whoever does not find comfort for his eye in Allah, his soul is cut to pieces by sorrows over the world. Allah, exalted is He, has only made the good life for those who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever does righteous deeds, male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. So He guaranteed for the people of faith and righteous deeds the reward in this world in the form of a good life, and the best reward on the Day of Resurrection. Thus they have the best of both lives, for they are alive in both abodes. A similar statement is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For those who do good in this world there is good, and the Home of the Hereafter is better, and excellent is the home of the righteous﴾ [al-Nahl: 30]. Similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that you ask forgiveness of your Lord and turn back to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term and will give every person of virtue his virtue﴾ [Hud: 3]. So the righteous and the doers of good triumphed with the bliss of this world and the Hereafter, and obtained the good life in both abodes. For the goodness of the soul, the joy and delight of the heart, its pleasure, its gladness, its tranquility, its expansion, its light, its ease and its well-being, which come from abandoning forbidden desires and false doubts, are truly bliss, and there is no comparison between bodily bliss and this. Some of those who tasted this pleasure used to say: 'If the kings and the sons of kings knew what we are in, they would fight us for it with swords.' Another said: 'There are times that pass over the heart in which I say: If the people of Paradise are in something like this, they are indeed in a good life.' Another said: 'In this world there is a paradise, which in this world is like the Paradise in the Hereafter. Whoever does not enter it does not enter the Paradise of the Hereafter.'"

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 20, verses 124–127 (part 3 of 4):

The Prophet (ﷺ) pointed to this Paradise in his saying: "When you pass by the gardens of Paradise, graze." They said: "What are the gardens of Paradise?" He said: "The circles of remembrance (dhikr)." He also said: "Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise." Do not think that the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ [al-Infitar: 13] ﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 14] are restricted to the Day of Return only. Rather, these (the righteous) are in bliss in their three abodes, and those (the wicked) are in the Fire in their three abodes. What pleasure and bliss in this world is more delightful than the righteousness of the heart, the soundness of the breast, knowledge of the Lord, the Exalted, love for Him, and acting in accordance with His pleasure? Is there any true life except the life of a sound heart? Allah the Exalted praised His intimate friend (khalil), peace be upon him, for the soundness of his heart, saying: ﴿Indeed, among those who followed his way was Abraham﴾ [al-Saffat: 83] ﴿When he came to his Lord with a sound heart﴾ [al-Saffat: 84]. He also related of him that he said: ﴿The Day when wealth and children will be of no benefit﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 88] ﴿except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 89]. The sound heart is the one that is free from shirk, rancour, malice, envy, stinginess, arrogance, the love of this world, and the desire for leadership. It is safe from every affliction that distances one from Allah, safe from every doubt that opposes His report, from every desire that opposes His command, and from every intention that competes with His purpose. It is safe from every obstacle that cuts one off from Allah. This sound heart is in a Paradise hastened in this world, in a Paradise in the barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection), and in the Paradise of the Day of Return. End, summarized.

(p-4227) He, may Allah have mercy on him, said in (Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah): Many of the salaf (the pious early generation) interpreted the words of the Exalted ﴿indeed, he will have a constricted life﴾ as referring to the punishment of the grave, and they took this verse as one of the proofs for the punishment of the grave. For this reason He said: ﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 125] ﴿He will say, "Thus did Our signs come to you, but you forgot them; and likewise today you are forgotten."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 126], meaning: you will be left in punishment just as you left acting upon Our signs. Thus He mentioned the punishment of the barzakh and the punishment of the abode of destruction (dar al-bawar). A parallel to this is His saying concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening﴾ [Ghafir: 46]. This refers to the barzakh. Then: ﴿And on the Day the Hour appears: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46]. This refers to the Greatest Resurrection. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels extend their hands, [saying]: "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and for being arrogant toward His signs."﴾ [al-An'am: 93]. The angels' words ﴿Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾ [al-An'am: 93] refer to the punishment of the barzakh, whose beginning is the day of seizing and death. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿If only you could see when those who disbelieved are taken by the angels, striking their faces and their backs, [saying]: "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ [al-Anfal: 50]. This tasting is in the barzakh, and its beginning is at the time of death, for it is joined to His saying: ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal: 50], and it is from the omitted speech (al-qawl al-mahdhuf), indicated by the context, as with its parallels. Both occur at the time of death.

In the Sahih, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27], he said: It was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave. The reports about the punishment of the grave nearly reach the level of tawatur (mass-transmission). The point is that Allah, glorified is He, informed that whoever turns away from His remembrance, which is the guidance that whoever follows will not go astray nor be miserable, has a constricted life. And He guarantees to whoever keeps His covenant that He will give him a good life and reward him in the Hereafter. He says: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. Thus He informed, glorified is He, of the success of whoever holds fast after it (the revelation) in knowledge and action, with a good life in this hastened world, and with the best reward in the Hereafter. This is the opposite of the one who has a constricted life in this world and in the barzakh, and who is forgotten in punishment in the Hereafter. He, glorified is He, also said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 36] ﴿And indeed, they (the devils) hinder them from the way, while they think they are guided﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 37]. He informed that his being afflicted with his devilish companion and his going astray because of him occurred only because of his turning away and his blindness to His remembrance, which He sent down upon His Messenger. Thus, the punishment for this turning away is that He appoints for him a devil who accompanies him, diverting him from the path of his Lord and the way of his success, while he thinks that he is guided. Until, when he comes to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection from his companion, and sees his ruin and bankruptcy, he says: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion!﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 38]. Everyone who turns away from being guided by the revelation, which is the remembrance of Allah, must say this on the Day of Resurrection.

If it is said: Does such a person have an excuse for his misguidance, if he thinks that he is upon guidance, as He said: ﴿And they think that they are guided﴾ [al-A'raf: 30]? It is said: There is no excuse for such a person and his likes in going astray, whose source of misguidance is turning away from the revelation that the Messenger brought. Even if he thinks he is guided, he is negligent by his turning away from following the caller to guidance. When he goes astray, he is only struck because of his negligence and his turning away. This differs from the one whose misguidance is due to the non-arrival of the message and his inability to reach it; for that one has a different ruling.

The threat in the Qur'an pertains only to the first. As for the second, Allah does not punish anyone except after the establishment of proof against him, as He said: ﴿And We never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15], and He said: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa: 165]. And He said concerning the people of the Fire: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were wrongdoers themselves﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 76]. And He said: ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Alas, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah, and indeed I was among the mockers"﴾ [al-Zumar: 56], or say ﴿"If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous"﴾ [al-Zumar: 57], or say when it sees the punishment ﴿"If only I had another chance, I would be among the good-doers"﴾ [al-Zumar: 58]. "Yes, indeed, My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers." This is frequent in the Qur'an.

Fifth: Ibn al-Qayyim said: There has been disagreement concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 124–125]: is it blindness of insight (basirah) or blindness of sight (basar)? Those who said it is blindness of insight were moved to that by His saying: ﴿How clearly they will hear and see on the day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38], and His saying: ﴿You were heedless of this, so We have removed your covering, and your sight today is sharp﴾ [Qaf: 22], and His saying: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no glad tidings that Day for the criminals﴾ [al-Furqan: 22], and His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire﴾ [al-Takathur: 6] ﴿Then you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾ [al-Takathur: 7], and similar verses that establish their sight in the Hereafter, and His saying: ﴿And you will see them presented to it, humbled by humiliation, looking with sidelong glances﴾ [al-Shura: 45], and His saying: ﴿The Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent push﴾ [al-Tur: 13] ﴿"This is the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ [al-Tur: 14] ﴿"Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?"﴾ [al-Tur: 15], and His saying: ﴿The criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53].

(p-4230) Those who preferred that it is blindness of sight said: The context indicates it, through His saying: ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 125]. He was never seeing in his disbelief at all. Rather, it became clear to him at that time that he had been in blindness to the truth in the world. So how could he say: ﴿while I was [once] seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha: 125], and how could he be answered with His saying: ﴿"Thus did Our signs come to you, but you forgot them"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 126]? Rather, this answer contains an indication that it is blindness of sight, and that he was recompensed in kind with his deed. For when he turned away from the remembrance with which Allah sent His Messenger, and his insight became blind to it, Allah blinded his sight on the Day of Resurrection and left him in punishment, just as he left the remembrance in the world. Thus He repaid him for the blindness of his insight with the blindness of his sight in the Hereafter, and for his leaving His remembrance, He left him in punishment. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whomever Allah guides is the one truly guided, and whomever He sends astray, you will not find for them protectors other than Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf﴾ [al-Isra: 97]. It has also been said concerning these verses that they are blind, mute, and deaf to guidance. Just as it has been said concerning this verse, ﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾, they said: because they will speak that day, and hear, and see.

As for one who holds that it is blindness, muteness, and deafness, which are opposed to sight, hearing, and speech, he said: it is a restricted, not absolute, blindness, deafness, and muteness. It is blindness to seeing what would please them and to hearing it. This has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "They will not see anything that pleases them." Others said: This gathering is when the angels take their souls; they leave the world in this state. When they rise from their graves to the place of standing (mawqif), they rise in this state. Then afterward they hear and see. This is narrated from al-Hasan.

Others said: This only happens when they enter the Fire and settle in it. Their hearing, sight, and speech are taken away, when the Lord, blessed and exalted, says to them: ﴿"Be silent in it, and do not speak to Me."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]. At that point hope is cut off, and their minds become mute, so they are seen all together, blind, mute, and deaf, neither seeing, nor hearing, nor speaking. Nothing is heard in it after that except the groaning and the wailing. This is related from Muqatil.

Those who said that what is meant is blindness to the argument (hujjah) meant only that they have no argument, and did not mean that they have an argument of which they are blind. Rather, they are blind to guidance as they were in the world. For a servant dies upon what he lived upon, and is resurrected upon what he died upon. By this it becomes clear that the correct view is the other opinion, that it is blindness of sight, and that the disbeliever will know the truth on the Day of Resurrection with direct vision, and will acknowledge what he used to deny in the world. So he is not blind to the truth on that Day.

The decisive matter (fasl al-khitab): gathering (hashr) means bringing together and assembling. It is sometimes used to mean gathering to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "You will be gathered to me barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised," and as in His saying: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [al-Takwir: 5], and His saying: ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ [al-Kahf: 47]. It is also used to mean bringing together and assembling to the abode of settlement. Thus the gathering of the righteous is their being assembled and brought together to Paradise, and the gathering of the disbelievers is their being assembled and brought together to the Fire. For He has informed us about them that they said: ﴿"Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment."﴾ [al-Saffat: 20] ﴿"This is the Day of Decision, which you used to deny."﴾ [al-Saffat: 21]. Then He said: ﴿"Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses"﴾ [al-Saffat: 22], and so on. This is the second gathering. Based on this, they are in the interval between the first gathering from the graves to the place of standing and the second gathering. They hear, see, dispute, and speak. At the second gathering they are gathered upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf. Every station has a state suited to it, which the justice and wisdom of the Lord, the Exalted, require. The Qur'an confirms its parts with one another: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much inconsistency﴾ [al-Nisa: 82]. End.

(p-4232) Sixth: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾ [Ta-Ha: 126], meaning: because you turned away from the signs of Allah and treated them as one who did not remember them after they reached you, you forgot them, turned away from them, and neglected them. Likewise today We treat you as one who forgets you: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day﴾ [al-A'raf: 51]. For the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. So forgetting here is a metaphor for abandoning.

Ibn Kathir said: As for forgetting the wording of the Qur'an while understanding its meaning and acting upon its requirements, it is not included in this specific threat. Yet it is threatened against from another angle, for the Sunnah has come with a emphatic prohibition and a severe warning concerning it.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No man recites the Qur'an and then forgets it, except that he will meet Allah on the day he meets Him, while he is leprous (ajdham)."

The seventh point: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus do We recompense those who transgress﴾ [Ta-Ha: 127], meaning: thus do We recompense those who exceed the limits and deny the signs of Allah, in this world and in the Hereafter. The punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting than the constricted life of this world, because it is everlasting. Then He, exalted is He, pointed to confirming what preceded regarding the arrival of the punishment, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted:

[128] ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect.﴾

﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾ — that is, to these deniers: ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾ — that is, the nations that denied the messengers: ﴿through whose dwellings they walk﴾ — he means the Quraysh; that is, they move about in the lands of ʿAd, Thamud and Lot and witness the traces of their destruction, and that there remains for them neither a lasting presence, nor an eye, nor a trace: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ — that is, the sound minds. As the Exalted said: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land, so that they would have hearts by which to understand or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts within the breasts.﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. And His, the Exalted, saying:

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[129] ﴿Were it not for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and an appointed term.﴾

﴿Were it not for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and an appointed term.﴾ This explains the wisdom behind delaying their punishment, along with the implication of His words: ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾ [Ta-Ha: 128] and so on, that He would destroy them like the destruction of those (earlier peoples), and the preceding word. Al-Qashani said: It is the prior decree that He would not uproot this nation with destruction and punishment in this world, because their Prophet is the Prophet of mercy. And His, glorified is He, words: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].

Al-Zamakhshari said: The preceding word is the promise to delay their recompense until the Hereafter. He says: Were it not for this promise, the like of our destruction of 'Ad and Thamud would have been inevitable for these disbelievers. Al-Lizam (inevitable, binding) is either a verbal noun of lazama (to cling, to be bound), like al-Khisam, described by it for emphasis; or an instrument noun, because things are fastened by it, like hizam (belt) and rikab (stirrup), and the instrument noun is likewise used as a description for emphasis, as in their saying: mis'ar harb (a kindler of war), and lizaz khasm, meaning one who presses hard upon his opponent, from lazza, meaning he constricted him.

Abu al-Baqa' permitted that it be the plural of lazim (binding), like qiyam, the plural of qa'im.

His, exalted is He, words: ﴿and an appointed term﴾ are coordinated with "word," meaning: Were it not for an appointed term for their lifespans or for their punishment, which is the Day of Resurrection or the Day of Badr, their punishment would not have been delayed at all.

Abu al-Su'ud said: Its separation from what it is conjoined to is for the indication that each of the two is independent, by negating that punishment is necessarily binding, and for observing the verse-endings of the noble verse.

It has also been permitted that it be conjoined to the pronoun hidden in (kana, "it would have been"), referring to the immediate seizure, which is understood from the context, treating the separation by the predicate as equivalent to emphasis. The meaning would be: "it would have been that the immediate seizure and an appointed term were both inevitable for them, like the custom of 'Ad, Thamud and their likes." The appointed term alone was not singled out apart from the immediate seizure. And His, exalted is He, words:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 20, verse 130:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[130] ﴿So be patient over what they say, and exalt [your Lord] with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night exalt Him, and at the ends of the day, that perhaps you may be pleased.﴾

﴿So be patient over what they say, and exalt [your Lord] with the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night exalt Him, and at the ends of the day, that perhaps you may be pleased.﴾ That is: since the delay of their punishment is not neglect but respite, then be patient over what they say of words of disbelief. The fa' here is causal (sababiyyah). By patience (sabr) is meant not being disturbed by what proceeds from them, not abandoning fighting, such that the verse would be abrogated (mansukh). Regarding the tasbih (glorification) commanded, there are two views:

The first: that it is tanzih (declaring God free of imperfection). The meaning: Exalt your Lord above associating partners with Him and all the deficiencies they attribute to Him, praising Him for having distinguished you with guidance, acknowledging that He is the master of all blessings. Among its transmitted formulas: "Glory be to God and by His praise." Accordingly, the specification of these times indicates continuity, although some times have a distinction by which they surpass others.

The second: that it is prayer (salah), and this is closest, due to the verse: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45], and the verses explain one another. The meaning: Pray while you are praising your Lord for His guidance and granting of success, before the rising of the sun, meaning the Fajr prayer. And before its setting, meaning the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, because they fall in the latter half of the day, between the decline of the sun and its setting. ﴿And during the hours of the night exalt Him﴾, that is, during its periods, meaning Maghrib and 'Isha'. The time is mentioned first for these two only because of their particular excellence. This is because the best remembrance is that which is done at night, due to the gathering of the heart, the calm of the foot, and being alone with the Lord, exalted is He. And because the night is a time of tranquility and rest; when it is devoted to worship, it is harder and more difficult upon the soul, and more exhausting and tiring for the body, so it is more excellent and closer to God.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾ is a repetition regarding the Fajr and Maghrib prayers, signalling that these two are specified with an additional excellence. Its coming in the plural form is to avoid confusion, and what is preferred is its harmony with "hours of the night." Or it commands the Zuhr prayer, for it is the end of the first half of the day and the beginning of the latter half. Its plural is considered in terms of the two halves. Or because "day" is a genus that includes every day, or it commands voluntary worship in parts of the day.

Al-Razi said: He commanded tasbih immediately after patience because the remembrance of God, exalted is He, brings consolation and rest, for there is no rest for the believers except in meeting God, exalted is He. I say: The wisdom of commanding patience and tasbih has been indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that perhaps you may be pleased﴾, that is, a hope that you may attain what your soul is pleased by: the raising of your mention, our subduing of your enemy for you, and reaching your aspiration of the manifestation of the tawhid of your Lord. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ [al-Isra': 79] and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be pleased﴾ [al-Duha: 5].

Then, exalted is He, indicated that what the disbelievers have been provided with of adornments is only a trial for them, so there should be no desire for it, and that what He has given you is greater and more exalted, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[131] ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.﴾

﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them﴾ — i.e., groups of the disbelievers. ﴿The splendor of the life of this world﴾ — i.e., its adornment. It is in the accusative either as a substitute (badal) for "azwajan" (pairs), or by "matta'na" (We have given enjoyment), with it being construed to carry the meaning of "a'ṭaynā" (We gave) and "khawwalnā" (We bestowed): ﴿that We may test them therein﴾ — i.e., that We may try them in what We have given them of that, and afflict them. Indeed, that is transient, perishing, a delusion and a deception that will vanish.

Abu al-Su'ud said: "that We may test them" is connected to "matta'na" (We have given enjoyment). It was brought to create aversion toward it by showing the evil of its final outcome, immediately after displaying its brilliance in its present state. That is: that We may deal with them as one who tests and examines them therein. Or: that We may punish them in the Hereafter because of it. ﴿But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾ — i.e., His reward in the Hereafter is better in itself than what they have been given enjoyment of, and more enduring, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Qasas: 80]. Or the meaning is: what you have been given of prophethood and guidance is better than what they have been tested with, and more lasting, because there is no comparison between the guidance which is followed by happiness in both abodes, and a flower one enjoys for a period and then it wilts and perishes.

In the expression "flower" there is an indication of the swiftness of its passing away, for its term is near. Among the subtleties of the verse is what al-Zamakhshari, may Allah have mercy on him, said, and his text is: "Extending the gaze" is lengthening it, and that one hardly returns it, out of admiration for the object looked at, and being impressed by it, and wishing that it were his. Like what the onlookers of Qarun did when they said: ﴿Would that we had the like of what Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune﴾ [al-Qasas: 79], until those given knowledge and faith confronted them with: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Qasas: 80].

And in it: that a glance which is not extended is pardoned. This is like the glance of one whom a thing overtakes with a look and then he lowers his gaze. And since looking at adornments is as if inherent in natures, and whoever sees something of them wants to extend his gaze toward it and fill his eyes with it, it was said: ﴿do not extend your eyes﴾ — i.e., do not do what you are accustomed to and what harms you. The scholars from among the people of piety have been strict regarding the obligation to lower the gaze from the buildings of the oppressors and the number of the wicked in clothing, vehicles, and other things, because they only adopted these things for the eyes of onlookers, so whoever looks at them is fulfilling their purpose, and is as one who incites them to adopt them. And His saying, exalted is He:

[132] ﴿And enjoin your family to pray, and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good end is for righteousness.﴾

﴿And enjoin your family to pray﴾: by "his family" is meant his household, or those who follow him. That is: command them to establish it, so that through it they draw their hearts toward the fear of God. ﴿And be steadfast in it﴾: that is, in performing it, so that through steadfastness in it he establishes in them the disposition (malakah) of firmness in worship, humility, and vigilance (muraqabah), from which every good results. Then God indicated that the command to it is only for the benefit and advantage of the one commanded, and that no benefit at all returns to the one who commands it, due to His exaltedness and transcendence, by His saying: ﴿We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you﴾: that is, We do not ask you for wealth. Rather, We impose on you a labor of your body, for which We will give you a great reward and abundant recompense. The meaning of "We provide for you" is: We give you wealth and make you earn, and We do not ask it of you. This is what Ibn Jarir said.

Abu Muslim said: The meaning is that God only desires worship from him and from them. He does not desire that he provide for Him, as masters desire kharaj (tribute) from slaves. This is like His saying: ﴿I did not create jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 56] ﴿I do not desire any provision from them, nor do I desire that they feed Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 57]. Some exegetes said: The meaning of the verse is: Turn with your family to prayer, and seek help through it against your need. Do not concern yourselves with the matter of provision and livelihood, for your provision is guaranteed from Us, and We are your providers. This meaning is not indicated by the verse either explicitly (manṭūq) or implicitly (mafhūm). It also encourages abstaining from earning, and provides a basis for the idle who are content to dwell in mosques instead of the striving that is commanded. God has said, describing the righteous: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God﴾ [An-Nur: 37], indicating their combining of the two virtues. ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 201].

His saying: ﴿And the good end is for righteousness﴾ means: the good outcome of every worker's deeds belongs to the people of righteousness and fear of God, not to those who fear no punishment from Him and hope for no reward from Him.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[133] ﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾

﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?"﴾ They mean the signs they were insolent in demanding, of the kind that preceded in Surat Bani Isra'il, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾ [al-Isra': 90] ﴿"or you have a garden of palms and grapevines"﴾ [al-Isra': 91].

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾, meaning: has there not come to them an explanation of what is in the books that came before this Book, of the reports of the nations before them, whom We destroyed when they asked for signs and then disbelieved in them after those signs came to them, how We hastened punishment upon them and sent down Our might upon them for their disbelief in them? The meaning is: what would assure them that, if the sign came to them, their condition would not be like the condition of those? This is what Ibn Jarir said.

Others held that the meaning is: has there not come to them a sign which is the mother of signs and the greatest of them, namely the miracle of the Qur'an, which explains what is in the earlier books of the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms? Although the one who brought it was unlettered, who had not seen them nor learned from those who knew them, so he selected from their reports what was sound, confirming it, and from what was false and distorted, refuting it. (p-4239) This also indicates the sufficiency of the revelation for miracle and proof, as He, exalted is He, said in Surat al-'Ankabut: ﴿And they say, "Why have signs not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 50] ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 51] For this reason one of the wise men of Islam said: The supernatural event on which Islam relies in its call to affirm the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ is the supernatural event whose report has been transmitted by mass narration (tawatur) and whose trace has not ceased. This alone is the proof. Whatever else has come in reports, whether its chain is sound, famous, weak, or fabricated, is not among what necessitates certainty for the Muslims. When it is cited in the context of argument, it is by way of strengthening the conviction for one whose foundation has been established, and an added confirmation for one from among its people who has accepted it. That mass-transmitted supernatural event upon which reliance is placed in argument to attain certainty is the Qur'an alone. The evidence that it is a miracle that breaks the normal course, indicating that its source is Allah alone and that it is not the invention of humans, is that it came through the tongue of an unlettered man who had not learned the Book nor practised the sciences; and it was revealed in a single measure, guiding the astray, rectifying the crooked, providing for a general order for the life of those among the nations who are guided by it, rescuing them from a loss they were in and a destruction they were about to fall into. And together with that, it is, in the eloquence of its style, beyond what any other speech has attained, to the point that the eloquent and the orators were challenged to produce something like it, and they were unable, and resorted to fighting with swords, shedding blood, and persecuting those who believed in it, until they compelled them to defend their right; and what occurred of it was the victory of truth over falsehood and the rising of the sun of Islam, extending its world with its lights and spreading its radiance across its atmosphere. This supernatural event has called people to consider it with their minds, and they were challenged to produce, by their own reckoning, the utmost that their power could reach; so if they found a way to nullify its miraculousness or to show that it is not fit to serve as proof for the claimant, then so be it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23], and He said: (p-4240) ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82], and He said other than that, which is a demand to counter argument with argument. He did not demand of them mere submission in spite of reason.

The miracle of the Qur'an is a combination of speech and knowledge, and each of them is something that the intellect grasps through understanding. It is a miracle that presented itself to the intellect, made it the judge therein, granted it the right to examine its aspects and to unfold what is folded within its folds, and it has from it its portion that is not diminished. It is a miracle that overwhelmed every capacity to produce its like, yet it called every power to take from it whatever it wishes. As for the miracle of the death of a living being without a known cause of death, or the return to life of a dead one, or the expulsion of a devil from a body, or the cure of an ailment from a body, these are matters before which the intellect halts and understanding stands still. Allah brings them only through His messengers, to silence peoples whom illusion overcame and whose minds were not illuminated by the light of knowledge. Thus Allah, by His power, establishes signs for the nations according to their capacities.

Another virtuous scholar said: The mercies of Allah, majestic is His glory, decreed that He form the existences in nature in a firmly ordered arrangement, which speaks with the tongue of silence to the discerning, appears in the garb of clarity to the reflective, and makes the passage from it to other things beloved to him without his feeling boredom or weariness, and he does not return from his insight with regret. Without this consideration by the intellect, it is not possible for the soul's belief to be sound, nor for it, as a consequence, to be calmed from its agitation. Moreover, we do not deny that a time passed over the human species in which the intellect was in the stage of childhood, and it sufficed for faith that one be astonished by a matter that breaks the natural order, suspending the course of its laws for a while. Allah, glorified and exalted, was merciful to His servants and sent to them messengers who endowed them with qualities whose secret their minds could not grasp, and their intellects were astonished by them; thus they took those miracles as proof of the Messenger's truthfulness and the necessity of following him. But now, since the intellect has reached its maturity and the human species its maturity of judgment, a miracle no longer benefits in it, and a strange wonder no longer profits in it, because doubts have multiplied along with the multiplication of scientific materials. If some such event occurs, they first accuse its doer of deception, then when his innocence of it becomes clear to them, they begin to explain away its miracle with every kind of explanation. This is on one side. On the other side, the sect of the Spiritualists (p-4241) in Europe now performs astonishing acts that break the laws of nature, which, if the ignorant saw them, they would think them among the greatest miracles, except that these people do not claim prophethood nor assert a mission. Yes, we do not deny that the works of this sect are not of the kind of the miracles of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, but it undoubtedly diminishes their importance in the eyes of those who stop at the surfaces of things.

Among what indicates that these latter centuries do not promote matters of miracles is the denial by the scholars of Europe of all previous miracles. This, though it is recklessness on their part, is nevertheless correct in their saying that we are in an age in which belief benefits nothing but the light of reason and scientific proof. For these reasons the Islamic law came calling to the true path, with the self-evident truths of reason and the principles of knowledge, turning attention away from miracles and the display of marvels, because Allah, glorified and exalted, knew that a time would come when scientific established facts would influence the rational faculty in ways that the breaking of natural laws would not influence it. End of quotation.

Then He, exalted is He, pointed to the ultimate purpose in sending the Messenger, may Allah's blessings be upon him, and the establishment of proof through his mission, by His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 20, verses 134–135:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[134] ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it [the Messenger], they would have said: "Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger, so that we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced."﴾ [135] ﴿Say: "Each is awaiting, so await. You will soon know who are the companions of the even path and who has been guided."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135].

﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, i.e., before the coming of the clear proof, or before Muhammad (peace be upon him): ﴿they would have said: "Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger, so that we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated"﴾, i.e., by the worldly punishment; ﴿and disgraced﴾, i.e., by the punishment of the Hereafter. That is: but We did not destroy them before its coming, so their excuse was cut off. Thereupon they said: ﴿"Yes, indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied him and said: 'Allah has not sent down anything.'"﴾ [al-Mulk: 9]. ﴿Say﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135], i.e., to those disbelieving rebels: ﴿Each﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135], i.e., of us and of you: ﴿is awaiting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135], i.e., waiting for what our affair and your affair will come to: ﴿so await. You will soon know﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135], i.e., soon: ﴿who are the companions of the even path﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135], i.e., the straight one: ﴿and who has been guided﴾ [Ta-Ha: 135], i.e., from deviation and misguidance. That is: is it the Prophet and his followers, or they and their followers?

Allah has fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, honored His army, and defeated the confederates by Himself alone. So to Him belongs all praise in the first and the last life.
